nearest_prior_work: Zsigmondy (1892) proves primitive prime divisors for a^n-b^n outside explicit classical exceptions.
Bilu, Hanrot, and Voutier (2001) prove eventual primitive divisors for Lucas and Lehmer sequences.
Those are producer theorems for structured sequences; the local theorem is only the downstream escape implication once bounded-degree order witnesses are already given.
classification.attribution: Attribute primitive-divisor context to Bang--Zsigmondy and its sequence generalizations. Describe the local theorem as an elementary Lean-checked transfer lemma, not as a primitive-divisor result.
classification.mathematical_interest: The abstraction cleanly exposes which input does the work: a uniform exponent bound converts divisibility by mq into a size lower bound on every occurring characteristic. The constant family C(n)=2 shows that cofinal nontriviality alone has no such force. The result merits a short producer-consumer-boundary segment, not a standalone theorem talk.
classification.reusable_scope: Any prime-indexed layer family in which every prime divisor admits a uniformly bounded exponent k with the layer index dividing p^k-1.
classification.why_it_matters: It turns the #249 algebraic route into a precise producer-consumer contract. The proof fleet must construct order witnesses and nontrivial layers; once those exist, finite-support escape and unbounded characteristic supply are already finished.

mechanism_comparison.primitive_divisor_producer: A Bang--Zsigmondy-type theorem proves that a structured sequence term has a prime divisor absent from earlier terms, typically forcing a large multiplicative order.
mechanism_comparison.local_transfer_consumer: The local theorem assumes every occurring p satisfies mq|p^k-1 for some k<=d. Hence mq<p^k, so any fixed p can occur only for bounded q; a finite union of such bounds gives finite-support escape.
mechanism_comparison.exact_delta: A structure-free, machine-checked consumer API that can accept order witnesses from cyclotomic, resultant, finite-field, or other algebraic producers.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: Without a producer proving nontrivial layers and the bounded-order certificates, the theorem yields no prime divisor at all.
